messages.subject: Sampling frequencies
parts:
Dear Dr Van Hees,

 

We still have some trouble with the sampling frequencies. Could you help us on the two following issues: 

  •        Which sampling frequency are you normally using to collect accelerometer data? Because with 100Hz you will get an error message in R due to memory issues.
  •        When the data is collected with 100Hz, are you then downsampling the data for the autocalibration to avoid this error message? And to which frequency would it be downsampled?

 

Thank you very much for your help!

 

Best regards,

Eric & Anne

messages.author: 8d92e34685fbc6bd
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Sampling frequencies
parts:
Dear Eric and Anne,

Are you working on a computer with low memory (< 8 GB of RAM?). Try setting argument chunksize to 0.5 ... or even lower if it still gives problems. This should address the memory issue.
Another approach is to switch to a computer with more memory: at least 8GB of RAM.
The sample frequency should not be the problem, GGIR can easily handle 100 Hertz sample rate.

Regards,
Vincent

Hi Eric & Anne, 

I just happened to come across this post. Hopefully you've been able to work out a solution by now, but if now, perhaps check your version of R/RStudio. I had these same issues early on even with 16GB RAM, but found that when I switched from the 32-bit to the 64-bit versions R and R Studio, everything worked much more smoothly without having to sacrifice chunk size. Best of luck! 

Scott
